newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips steady, SAX edges higher.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips steady, SAX edges higher.

text.p: Major Slovak shares held steady in light trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with minor gains to several highly-capitalised issues helping the SAX index firm 0.18 points to 207.02.
Steel maker VSZ traded the largest volume among the listed blue chips, 1,236 shares, rising five crowns to 715.
Brokers said VSZ had potential to rise equal to levels where a domestic shareholder sold a block of the shares last week.
"There is still demand for VSZ at the moment, which coupled with a lack of its shares on the offer could push the issue to at least 740 crowns," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Oil refiner Slovnaft firmed 10 crowns to close at 1,010.
"The demand and offer could now meet at some 1,015 crowns, but, again, lack of liquidity can pull the share's price higher soon," Sykora said.

Trading has been very quiet over the past week, but broker said that foreign investors, who are the only players to give the market impetus for a longer-term trend, may soon return to pick up some undervalued shares.
"They can come out of the blue, as, for example, VSZ or Slovnaft appear to be the region's cheapest shares in their field," Sykora said.
Overall volume fell to 196,577 shares, from 334,101 stocks on Wednesday and the turnover eased to 170.21 million crowns, from 221.40 million.
